title: Traffic Signs: Shapes, Colours & Meanings
whatItIs: Three basic types of sign: circles give orders, triangles warn, rectangles inform. Colour is a further guide. STOP and GIVE WAY break the shape rules so they stand out.
keyFacts: A red ring or red circle shows a prohibition: what you must not do.
A blue circle (no red border) mostly gives a positive instruction, or marks a route for certain vehicles only.

keyFacts.text: You MUST obey traffic signs giving orders, including temporary signs.
At a STOP sign you MUST stop before the line and make sure the way is clear before entering the major road.

keyFacts: All triangular signs are red. Plates below a sign qualify its message, e.g. a time plate.
Direction signs: blue on motorways, green on primary routes, white on other routes, brown for tourist sites.

visual.caption: Circle = order · triangle = warning · rectangle = information

a.label: Red ring or circle
points: Prohibition: what you must not do
e.g. no entry, maximum speed, no U-turns

b.label: Blue circle
points: Or a route only for some traffic, e.g. cycles

onTheTest.question: A pupil asks what a blue circular sign with no red border generally tells them. Which answer is correct?
options: A hazard on the road ahead
A restriction that applies only at certain times
onTheTest.why: Know Your Traffic Signs: blue circles generally give a mandatory instruction, such as 'turn left', or show a route only for particular classes of traffic, such as buses and cycles.

onTheTest.question: Why do the STOP and GIVE WAY signs not follow the normal shape and colour rules?
options: Because they only apply at night
onTheTest.why: Know Your Traffic Signs says there are a few exceptions to the shape and colour rules, to give certain signs greater prominence. The STOP and GIVE WAY signs are the examples.

traps: Blue rectangles are information signs, except on motorways, where blue is used for direction signs.
No upright GIVE WAY sign? On quiet junctions the sign, or both sign and road triangle, may be left out.
A time plate under a 'no right turn' or 'no left turn' sign makes it a part-time ban: read the plate.
